text: Profound geoeconomic shifts, housing shortages, energy bottlenecks, and a persistent productivity gap between domestic firms and MNEs call for structural reforms to safeguard Ireland’s competitiveness. Key policy targets include delivering 300,000 homes for 2025–2030, rental sector reforms starting 1 March 2026, and 90 deliverables across seven policy areas under the digital strategy. IMF staff warns that rapid AI technology risks further widening the productivity divide, and recommends removing rent controls, streamlining planning processes, reinforcing electricity grid infrastructure, broadening carbon pricing, and advancing the SIU and 28th regime.
